result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers agree that the forced tour is wrong and offer similar alternatives: in-place hints, a command palette, behavior-triggered nudges and a task-grouped cheat sheet. A is slightly better because it teaches the first few shortcuts inside real work and makes the full walkthrough an opt-in option in Help. B still puts a short interactive exercise on day one and adds weekly tips that drift toward calendar nudges. Neither is especially compact, but A's pitch to the PM is tighter and easier to act on. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers agree with the user and propose similar contextual approaches: hints in the UI, a command palette, behavior-triggered nudges and a grouped cheat sheet. B ties its reasons more closely to these users: billable time makes a tour feel like a tax, and it borrows conventions from Word and Outlook. B also says to pick the starter shortcuts using usage data and explicitly makes the full walkthrough opt-in, off the default path. Both are fairly long for something to bring to a PM, and B's extra point about shortcut design adds a little length but is useful.
